title: Five native TTS generation results; speaker timing pending
scope: Five completed native generated-PCM comparisons plus a prepared separate physical speaker-start collector.
summary: All five generation results are saved individually. Speaker output and ASR-plus-voice qualification remain pending; no fastest-audible default has been selected.

environment.workload: One engine/model process at a time

provenance.kind: Progress summary; see individually registered native engine runs and retained report

limitations: Generated PCM timings are separate from actual non-silent render, estimated presentation and microphone-observed pickup.
The speaker collector has authored native controls, including an original/fixed maximum-latency search regression; physical model collection awaits a coordinated optimized app build.
One disposable TTS model/process at a time; each result is saved and its owned model removed before proceeding.
Full-turn speech-end/ASR/EOU, physical route matrix, voice quality and default qualification remain open.

method: Known English text is sent through the actual native voice adapter after preparation. Five back-to-back warm same-text requests are summarized separately from the first synthesis after preparation.
The clock stops at the first nonempty generated PCM buffer. It does not stop at a speaker, a microphone, or the end of a conversational turn.
findings: All five generation results are saved individually. Speaker output and ASR-plus-voice qualification remain pending; no fastest-audible default has been selected.
Generated audio can be ready before playback starts. Use the separate physical speaker reports before drawing a conclusion about how quickly someone hears this voice.
report.purpose: How quickly can this voice produce its first usable audio buffer? This isolates generation from the separate wait for playback and sound.
